Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint NAS-HPO framework consistently outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability. These results highlight the benefits of jointly optimizing model structure and training dynamics for scalable and effective RL agent design.
tldr: This paper introduces a dual-branch evolutionary framework that jointly optimizes neural network architectures and hyperparameters for reinforcement learning policies in autonomous driving, demonstrating improved reward, efficiency, and stability over standalone NAS in a high-fidelity simulator.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种双分支进化框架，在自动驾驶强化学习策略中联合优化神经网络架构和超参数，实验表明其在模拟器中比单独NAS获得更高奖励、更少参数和更好的稳定性。
summary_zh: 在本研究中，我们提出了一种双分支进化框架，该框架在自动驾驶任务中的强化学习（RL）中同时执行神经架构搜索（NAS）和超参数优化（HPO）。尽管NAS在自动化卷积神经网络（CNNs）架构设计方面展现出巨大潜力，但其在强化学习中的应用仍然有限，尤其是在需要联合优化架构与训练动态的场景中。基于我们先前在进化多目标神经架构搜索（EMNAS）方面的工作，所提出的框架在统一的多目标搜索策略下，并行进化离散网络架构和连续超参数。在此设置中，NAS针对强化学习策略网络中的卷积层——负责视觉特征提取——而HPO则专注于优化关键的强化学习超参数。为加速收敛并提升泛化能力，我们引入了并行评估和师生策略迁移机制。在高保真驾驶模拟器中的实验表明，联合NAS-HPO框架持续优于单独使用NAS的方法，生成的策略具有更高的奖励、更少的参数以及更好的稳定性。这些结果凸显了联合优化模型结构与训练动态对于可扩展且高效的强化学习智能体设计的优势。

title: Predict the Swing, Match the Speed: Robotic Pipe Stabbing With Learned Stereo Vision and Residual Reinforcement Learning
summary: A joint of pipe run into the hole swings from the elevator over the well and strikes a fixed stabbing guide at whatever speed the swing has. StabBot, a robotic stabbing system, predicts the swing and meets the pipe at its own speed. A pendulum Kalman filter tuned from the pipe tally tracks the joint in stereo images. A six-axis arm with an open V-shaped roller head closes in at matched velocity, confirms the last millimetres by touch, aims the pin over the box when the elevator hangs off centre, and follows the block down with lateral compliance. A ResNet-18 keypoint network locates the pipe, pin nose and box mouth in 3-D, and a residual reinforcement-learning policy refines the capture. On 200 paired random jobs with nine sizes from 2-3/8-in. tubing to 20-in. casing, StabBot seated every joint with the pipe touching only rollers, against 74% for a conventional fixed guide. Median contact speed fell from 18.4 to 2.3 cm/s and median peak head-pipe force from 11.3 to 1.4 kN, and the force was lower in all 200 jobs (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-30}$). The network locates the pipe with 0.4-mm median error in 2.3 ms per stereo pair. With the network in the loop, success stayed at 100% under 20 mm of added noise, 300-ms delay, 85% frame loss, 20-mm calibration offset, 20-cm elevator offset and 40-cm swings. All results come from a 1:4 Froude-scaled MuJoCo model and are reported at full scale.
tldr: StabBot uses learned stereo vision (ResNet-18 keypoints) and residual reinforcement learning to predict pipe swing and match velocity during robotic pipe stabbing in oil drilling, achieving 100% success in simulation with lower contact forces and robustness to disturbances compared to a fixed guide.
tldr_zh: StabBot利用学习到的立体视觉（ResNet-18关键点）和残差强化学习在石油钻井过程中预测管道摆动并匹配速度，在仿真中实现了100%的成功率，且接触力更低，对干扰具有鲁棒性，优于固定导向器。
summary_zh: 摘要：下井管柱接头从井口上方的大钩中摆动，并以摆动速度撞击固定的对扣导向装置。StabBot（一种机器人对扣系统）可预测摆动，并以自身速度迎接管柱。基于管柱记录调校的摆锤卡尔曼滤波器在立体图像中跟踪接头。六轴机械臂配备开放式V形滚轮头，以匹配速度接近，通过触觉确认最后几毫米位置，在大钩偏心悬挂时将公扣对准母扣，并以横向柔顺性随游车下移。ResNet-18关键点网络在三维空间中定位管柱、公扣尖端和母扣口，残差强化学习策略进一步优化抓取动作。在200次成对随机作业中，涵盖从2-3/8英寸油管到20英寸套管的9种规格，StabBot在管柱仅接触滚轮的情况下实现了每次接头的成功对扣，而传统固定导向装置的成功率为74%。中位接触速度从18.4 cm/s降至2.3 cm/s，中位峰值头管力从11.3 kN降至1.4 kN，且在全部200次作业中该力均更低（Wilcoxon检验p < 10⁻³⁰）。该网络在每对立体图像上以2.3 ms的处理时间实现0.4 mm的中位定位误差。在加入20 mm噪声、300 ms延迟、85%帧丢失、20 mm标定偏移、20 cm大钩偏移及40 cm摆动的条件下，网络闭环下的成功率仍保持100%。所有结果均来自1:4弗劳德缩比MuJoCo模型，并以全尺寸报告。

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
summary: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.
tldr: This paper introduces MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that co-adapts a hip-exoskeleton control policy with a musculoskeletal human model in simulation, trained with a metabolic-energy reward. The learned policy reduces metabolic cost in new users without per-user tuning, demonstrating successful sim-to-real transfer.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了MARL-Exo，一种多智能体强化学习框架，在仿真中与肌肉骨骼人体模型共同适应训练髋部外骨骼控制策略，并使用代谢能量奖励。该策略无需个体调参即可降低新用户的代谢成本，展示了成功的仿真到现实迁移。
summary_zh: 目的：本研究旨在探究在模拟环境中，通过肌肉骨骼人体模型与代谢能量奖励的协同适应训练得到的髋部外骨骼控制策略，能否在无需个体化调整的情况下，降低新用户行走的代谢能耗，并分析机械功率塑形对学习到的辅助模式有何影响。方法：我们开发了MARL-Exo，一种多智能体强化学习框架，其中包含全身人体模型（304个肌肉驱动器；随机化解剖结构、步态和速度）和双侧髋部外骨骼控制策略，两者分两个阶段同步训练。外骨骼仅观察延迟的髋部运动学信息及其历史指令；其奖励包括基于生理能量模型的肌肉代谢功率，单独使用（代谢组）或结合机械功率塑形（代谢+功率组）。代谢组策略在未经重新训练的情况下，部署并测试于8名健康成年人以1.25 m/s速度行走的场景中，采用间接测热法评估效果。结果：在模拟中，代谢组策略相比无设备行走，将模型肌肉代谢功率降低了13.8%，而代谢+功率组仅降低了8.8%。在硬件实验中，MARL-Exo使所有8名参与者的净代谢率相比被动组降低了18.3 ± 6.6%。相比无外骨骼组，平均降低幅度为7.4 ± 10.0%；其中6名参与者不仅完全抵消了13.1%的设备穿戴负担，其代谢能耗甚至低于无外骨骼状态，最高降幅达24.2%。结论：在模拟中协同适应得到的代谢信息驱动策略，无需个体化调整即可迁移至实际使用者，并持续降低穿戴设备行走的代谢能耗；而显式的功率塑形反而削弱了模拟中的辅助收益。意义：与依赖个体在环优化的方法不同，本方法能够生成单一群体级控制策略，并允许在人体测试之前，于模拟环境中对辅助目标进行筛选评估。

title: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios
summary: Modern simulators can generate synthetic camera and LiDAR data with accurate annotations for downstream tasks. In contrast, automotive radar simulation remains less mature because it requires not only a 3D engine to model dynamic objects in the scenes but also electromagnetic material properties, antenna configurations, wave propagation mechanisms, and coherent signal synthesis. Existing frameworks are either proprietary or overly simplified, limiting the scalability of radar raw measurements. This paper presents AuRaSim, a ray-tracing-based automotive frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar simulation framework for dynamic scenarios. Rather than implementing all components from scratch, AuRaSim builds on Blender for efficient dynamic-scene construction and Sionna RT for graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated electromagnetic ray tracing, while introducing radar-specific adaptations for path-resolved propagation with complex coefficients, motion-aware Doppler modeling, and subsequently coherent multi-channel analog-to-digital converter (ADC) cube synthesis based on waveform configurations. Quantitative comparison between simulated and measured range-Doppler maps in digital-twin scenarios achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.147 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 16.93 dB, demonstrating the accuracy and fidelity of the synthetic signal. AuRaSim therefore provides a complete and extensible platform for reproducible automotive radar simulation and research. Project homepage: https://wangzhaoze.github.io/aurasim.
tldr: AuRaSim is a ray-tracing-based automotive FMCW radar simulator for dynamic scenarios, built on Blender and Sionna RT, that can synthesize coherent ADC cubes and is validated against measured data in digital-twin scenarios.
tldr_zh: AuRaSim 是一个基于光线追踪的汽车 FMCW 雷达模拟器，适用于动态场景，基于 Blender 和 Sionna RT 构建，可合成相干 ADC 数据立方体，并在数字孪生场景中与实测数据进行了验证。
summary_zh: 现代仿真器能够为下游任务生成带有精确标注的合成相机和激光雷达数据。相比之下，车载雷达仿真仍不够成熟，因为它不仅需要三维引擎来对场景中的动态目标进行建模，还需要考虑电磁材料特性、天线配置、波传播机制以及相干信号合成。现有框架要么是专有的，要么过于简化，限制了雷达原始测量的可扩展性。本文提出了AuRaSim，一种基于射线追踪的车载调频连续波（FMCW）雷达仿真框架，适用于动态场景。AuRaSim并非从头实现所有组件，而是基于Blender构建高效的动态场景，并利用Sionna RT进行图形处理单元（GPU）加速的电磁射线追踪，同时引入针对雷达的特定适配，包括带复系数的路径分辨传播、运动感知多普勒建模，以及基于波形配置的相干多通道模数转换器（ADC）数据立方体合成。在数字孪生场景中，仿真与实测距离-多普勒图的定量比较实现了0.147的均方根误差（RMSE）和16.93 dB的峰值信噪比（PSNR），证明了合成信号的准确性和逼真度。因此，AuRaSim为可重复的车载雷达仿真与研究提供了一个完整且可扩展的平台。项目主页：https://wangzhaoze.github.io/aurasim。

title: State estimation for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator system
summary: Spacecraft-mounted robotic manipulators can support long-term operability of orbiting assets by conducting tasks such as on-orbit assembly, repair, upgrade, and refueling. In this context, the integration of continuum/soft robotic mechanisms into space manipulator designs promises to reduce stowage volume and mass, as well as to improve operational safety through the inherent mechanical compliance of soft structures. This work presents a novel state reconstruction pipeline for a hybrid soft-rigid space manipulator, in which the distal link is a tendon-driven continuum robot. The estimation problem is formulated as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference problem over the hybrid manipulator's configuration, conditioned on discrete, noisy measurements from joint encoders and a vision-based sensing pipeline. The resulting soft-constrained optimization problem is transcribed as a factor graph, providing a compact representation for fusing heterogeneous measurements with the rigid-soft kinematic model. Furthermore, the adoption of the Geometric Variable Strain (GVS) approach yields a minimum-order parameterization of the configuration, a property expected to facilitate model-based feedback control design in future work. The proposed implementation is validated in simulation on a closed-loop trajectory where, for better realism, position measurements for the continuum link are obtained by means of a simulated visual pipeline leveraging synthetic photorealistic images. The state reconstruction accuracy and computational performance confirm the potential of the proposed framework for hybrid soft-rigid robotic applications in orbit.
tldr: This paper presents a state estimation pipeline for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator, formulated as MAP inference on a factor graph with GVS-based parameterization, validated in simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种混合刚柔太空机械臂的状态估计流程，基于因子图上的MAP推断和GVS参数化，并在仿真中验证。
summary_zh: 安装在航天器上的机械臂可以通过执行在轨装配、维修、升级和加注等任务，为轨道资产提供长期可操作性支持。在此背景下，将连续体/软体机器人机制集成到空间机械臂设计中，有望减小收纳体积和质量，并通过软体结构的固有机械柔顺性提高操作安全性。本文提出了一种针对混合软-刚体空间机械臂的新型状态重建方法，其中末端连杆为由腱驱动连续体机器人。该估计问题被表述为混合机械臂构型上的最大后验（MAP）推断问题，其条件基于关节编码器和基于视觉的传感管道提供的离散、含噪测量数据。由此产生的软约束优化问题被转化为因子图，为将异构测量数据与刚-柔运动学模型融合提供了一种紧凑表示方式。此外，采用几何变应变（GVS）方法实现了构型的最小阶参数化，这一特性预计将有助于未来工作中基于模型的反馈控制设计。所提出的实现方法在闭环轨迹上进行了仿真验证，为提高逼真度，连续体连杆的位置测量通过利用合成逼真图像的模拟视觉管道获得。状态重建精度和计算性能证实了所提出框架在轨混合软-刚体机器人应用中的潜力。

title: Camera-to-Quadruped Robot Pose Estimation from Sequential Images
summary: Quadruped robots are increasingly deployed in hazardous environments such as disaster response and facility inspection, where external-camera monitoring is essential for safe operation. This setting is challenging because quadrupeds are articulated systems with time-varying leg joints, leg symmetry, and frequent self-occlusions, which make keypoint correspondence ambiguous. Moreover, no public benchmark exists, making quantitative comparison difficult. To address these challenges, we propose QuadPose, which estimates the full-body 18-DoF pose (6-DoF base pose + 12-DoF joint angles) from monocular video sequences, and introduce QuadSyn, the first camera-to-quadruped robot pose benchmark. On QuadSyn, QuadPose achieves 92.18% PCK@2.5px, 95.54% PCK-AUC, 85.94% ADD@20cm, 66.98% ADD-AUC, and 3.65 degree mean joint-angle error at approximately 33 FPS.
tldr: Introduces QuadPose, a monocular video-based method for full-body 18-DoF pose estimation of quadruped robots, along with QuadSyn, the first benchmark for this task. Achieves high accuracy on the new benchmark at real-time speed.
tldr_zh: 提出QuadPose，一种基于单目视频的四足机器人全身18自由度姿态估计方法，并引入首个相关基准QuadSyn。该新基准上达到高精度且实时运行。
summary_zh: 四足机器人正越来越多地被部署在危险环境中，例如灾害响应和设施巡检，在这些场景中，外部摄像头监控对于安全操作至关重要。这一环境具有挑战性，因为四足机器人是带有随时间变化的腿部关节、腿部对称性以及频繁自遮挡的关节系统，这使得关键点对应关系变得模糊不清。此外，目前尚无公开基准，导致定量比较困难。为解决这些挑战，我们提出了QuadPose，它能够从单目视频序列中估计全身18自由度姿态（6自由度基座姿态+12自由度关节角度），并引入了QuadSyn，这是首个相机到四足机器人姿态基准。在QuadSyn上，QuadPose取得了92.18%的PCK@2.5px、95.54%的PCK-AUC、85.94%的ADD@20cm、66.98%的ADD-AUC，以及约33帧/秒速度下3.65度的平均关节角度误差。

title: Bridging Exploration and Loss of Plasticity in On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have been observed to lose the ability to adaptively learn from new data, a phenomenon termed Loss of Plasticity (LoP). While many metrics have been shown to correlate with it, the causal mechanisms and the geometric conditions from which it can arise have not been clearly identified. We analyze LoP in Proximal Policy Optimization with isotropic Gaussian policies, the state-of-the-art formulation for many continuous action spaces in RL. We report multiple metrics which characterize the effect that the policy standard deviation $σ$ has on LoP, and we also suggest related explanations for the effectiveness of widely adopted LoP mitigation techniques. We observe a significant effect of $σ$ on the extent of LoP, and accompany this with both theoretical and experimental supporting arguments. Our experimental validation consists of LoP benchmark evaluations against standard baselines as well as real-world policy deployment on a 7-DoF robotic arm.
tldr: This paper investigates the loss of plasticity in on-policy RL, focusing on the role of policy standard deviation in PPO, and validates findings with real-world deployment on a 7-DoF robotic arm.
tldr_zh: 本文研究了在线策略强化学习中的可塑性丧失问题，重点关注PPO中策略标准差的作用，并通过在7自由度机械臂上的实际部署验证了结论。
summary_zh: 深度强化学习算法已被观察到会丧失从新数据中进行适应性学习的能力，这一现象被称为可塑性丧失（Loss of Plasticity，简称LoP）。尽管已有许多度量指标被证明与其相关，但其因果机制及可能引发该现象的几何条件尚未被明确识别。我们针对采用各向同性高斯策略的近端策略优化（Proximal Policy Optimization）算法分析了LoP，该策略形式是强化学习中许多连续动作空间的最新表述。我们报告了多个度量指标，用以刻画策略标准差$σ$对LoP的影响，并提出了对广泛采用的LoP缓解技术有效性的相关解释。我们观察到$σ$对LoP程度具有显著影响，并辅以理论与实验两方面的支持性论证。我们的实验验证包括针对标准基准的LoP基准评估，以及在七自由度机械臂上的实际策略部署。

title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security
summary: Coding agents can adapt robotic software by revising executable programs, but successful responses to an evolving opponent may not remain effective. We present a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Environment-specific interfaces support external programs for autonomous driving and SDK-level defenses for humanoid locomotion. Two eight-generation case studies reveal concrete software responses: a driving defender introduces direct-actuation recovery, while a humanoid defender revises incoming-state validation. These responses provide local task recovery but do not establish sustained robustness. The framework makes such adaptation and limitations observable through executable artifacts and task-level evidence.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play, where coding agents generate attacks and defenses for robotic software, demonstrated on autonomous driving and humanoid locomotion, revealing local task recovery but limited sustained robustness.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一个程序级对抗性共同适应自博弈框架，让编码代理为机器人软件生成攻击和防御，并在自动驾驶和人形运动上进行了验证，结果显示局部任务恢复能力，但缺乏持续的鲁棒性。
summary_zh: 编码智能体可通过修订可执行程序来适配机器人软件，然而针对不断演化的对手所取得的成功响应未必能持续有效。我们提出了一种程序级对抗性协同自适应自博弈框架，在该框架中，编码智能体基于经过测试的对手代码与任务反馈生成攻击与防御策略，且无需模型微调。环境专属接口支持自动驾驶的外部程序以及人形运动学的SDK级防御。两项八代案例研究揭示了具体的软件响应行为：自动驾驶防御方引入了直接驱动恢复机制，而人形防御方则修正了输入状态验证逻辑。这些响应能够实现局部任务恢复，但未能建立起持续稳健性。该框架通过可执行工件与任务级证据，使此类适应过程及其局限性得以可观察化。

title: GCSR-OCC: Geometry Calibration and Semantic Routing for Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Prediction
summary: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction represents scene geometry and semantics in a unified voxel grid, enabling recognition beyond predefined categories. One approach reconstructs scenes with 3D Gaussians and converts them into voxel occupancy. However, Gaussian scale inflation and excessive overlap can distort voxel occupancy predictions, while semantic mixing can arise within Gaussians spanning multiple categories and during 3D--2D semantic feature alignment. We propose GCSR-OCC, which combines geometry calibration and multi-mode query-conditioned semantic routing for indoor occupancy prediction from a single RGB image. The Evidence-Conserving Gaussian-to-Occupancy operator (EC-G2O) uses kernel mass normalization, $p$-norm aggregation, and a learnable gain to suppress scale inflation and excessive local evidence accumulation while calibrating occupancy responses. Multi-mode Query-First Gaussian Semantic Routing (MM-QGSR) matches multiple semantic modes per Gaussian to text queries and aggregates query-specific evidence into voxels through a learnable text-conditioned router. Fine-grained subclass queries and smoothed semantic aggregation further refine voxel-level predictions. Without 3D semantic annotations, GCSR-OCC achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary occupancy prediction on Occ-ScanNet, with 63.31% geometric IoU and 27.44% semantic mIoU. It also reduces geometric aggregation latency from 19.76 ms to 12.88 ms. Our code will be made publicly available.
tldr: GCSR-OCC proposes geometry calibration and semantic routing methods for open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction from a single RGB image, achieving state-of-the-art on Occ-ScanNet without 3D semantic annotations.
tldr_zh: GCSR-OCC 提出了几何校准和语义路由方法，用于从单张 RGB 图像进行开放词汇 3D 占用预测，在没有 3D 语义标注的情况下，在 Occ-ScanNet 上取得了最先进的性能。
summary_zh: 开放词汇3D占用预测在统一体素网格中表示场景几何与语义，能够识别预定义类别之外的物体。一种方法是用3D高斯重建场景并将其转换为体素占用。然而，高斯尺度膨胀和过度重叠会扭曲体素占用预测，同时跨多个类别的高斯以及在3D-2D语义特征对齐过程中可能产生语义混合问题。我们提出GCSR-OCC，结合几何校准与多模式查询条件语义路由，从单张RGB图像实现室内占用预测。证据守恒高斯到占用算子（EC-G2O）通过核质量归一化、$p$-范数聚合和可学习增益来抑制尺度膨胀和局部证据过度累积，同时校准占用响应。多模式查询优先高斯语义路由（MM-QGSR）将每个高斯的多种语义模式与文本查询匹配，并通过可学习的文本条件路由器将查询特定证据聚合到体素中。细粒度子类查询和平滑语义聚合进一步细化体素级预测。在没有3D语义标注的情况下，GCSR-OCC在Occ-ScanNet上的开放词汇占用预测中达到最先进性能，几何IoU为63.31%，语义mIoU为27.44%。同时，几何聚合延迟从19.76毫秒降至12.88毫秒。我们的代码将公开发布。

title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
summary: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.
tldr: This paper investigates spatiotemporal intelligence in foundation vision models using egocentric tennis videos, evaluating seven prediction tasks and proposing a conditional diffusion model for real-time kinematic motion generation. It finds that depth information improves 3D ball localization and that scene context, rather than long image histories, is key for forecasting.
tldr_zh: 本文利用自我中心的网球视频研究基础视觉模型在时空智能方面的能力，评估了七项预测任务，并提出了一种用于实时运动生成的扩散模型。研究发现深度信息对3D球定位至关重要，且场景上下文而非长图像历史是预测的关键。

title: Leveraging Distributed Sensing and Hyperdimensional Computing for Non-Line-of-Sight Passive Object Sensing
summary: In smart factory environments, passive entities such as humans and movable obstacles may interfere with autonomous robot operations, posing significant safety risks. Detecting potential conflicts between robots and entities outside their field-of-view (FoV) is therefore of paramount importance. However, conventional passive object detection systems rely on sensors such as LiDAR, radar, or cameras, which operate under direct line-of-sight (LoS) and are limited by obstacles and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables environmental perception via the communication infrastructure thanks to cooperation among distributed wireless devices. In this paper, we propose a framework for passive entity sensing beyond the robot's FoV that relies solely on distributed channel measurements from the communication infrastructure to perform risk-aware classification. These measurements are embedded into high-dimensional representations using hyperdimensional computing (HDC), enabling robust and scalable learning without explicit channel reconstruction. Numerical simulations based on a commercial ray tracer and ROS-based validation in realistic smart factory scenarios demonstrate improved safety and enhanced path planning with up to 89% accuracy under severe occlusions, while maintaining low computational complexity.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework using distributed wireless channel measurements and hyperdimensional computing to enable passive sensing of entities beyond a robot's field-of-view in smart factories, improving safety and path planning.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种利用分布式无线信道测量和超维度计算实现智能工厂中机器人视野外被动实体感知的框架，以提高安全性和路径规划。

title: Spiking Neuromorphic Control for Periodic Orbits Stabilization in Underactuated Robots: A Greedy Lyapunov-Based Approach
summary: This work investigates the use of event-based spiking controllers, implemented as spiking neural networks, for trajectory tracking in underactuated robots. Specifically, we address the problem of stabilizing a prescribed periodic orbit. It is well known that, by applying the method of transverse linearization to the robot dynamics in a neighborhood of a periodic trajectory, the dynamics can be approximately described by a linear time-varying system with periodic coefficients (a periodic LTV system). The problem of orbital stabilization can therefore be reduced to stabilizing the trivial solution of this LTV system. We show that a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design, originally developed for LTI systems, can also be extended to the corresponding linearized transverse dynamics, which take the form of a periodic LTV system. This enables the construction of a feedback controller for orbital stabilization of the robot. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on the trajectory stabilization problem for the butterfly robot.
tldr: This paper extends a Lyapunov-based greedy design to periodic LTV systems for orbital stabilization of underactuated robots using spiking neural network controllers, demonstrated on a butterfly robot.
tldr_zh: 本文将基于李雅普诺夫贪心设计扩展到周期线性时变系统，用于欠驱动机器人周期轨道稳定的脉冲神经网络控制，并在蝴蝶机器人上验证。

title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
summary: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. Despite numerous prior works on ground robots, aerial robots with high agility and constrained sensor suites face more significant localization drift and thereby demand dedicated active SLAM planning. Moreover, a unified strategy that adapts performance based on task-specific priorities remains an open question. In this article, we introduce RAVEN, a unified active SLAM framework for Rapid Autonomous Visual ExploratioN using quadrotors, which systematically accounts for localization uncertainty. The framework starts with identifying frontiers and active loop closure candidates, from which global tour candidates are generated. These candidates are evaluated using a utility vector that separately quantifies exploration efficiency and localization accuracy, and the final tour is selected according to a prioritization parameter ranging from $[0,1]$. Finally, a perception-aware navigation planner generates smooth execution trajectories that minimize visual state estimation error based on the online Fisher information field that provides visual localization information in real-time. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that RAVEN outperforms state-of-the-art active SLAM methods, highlighting its advantages in producing a spectrum of performance across prioritizations. Fully onboard field experiments with a customized stereo-inertial quadrotor further validate its practical applicability in challenging environments. The source code will be released to benefit the community.
tldr: RAVEN presents a unified active SLAM framework for quadrotors that balances exploration and localization accuracy via a prioritization parameter, validated in benchmarks and onboard field experiments.
tldr_zh: RAVEN 提出了一种用于四旋翼飞行器的统一主动 SLAM 框架，通过优先级参数平衡探索与定位精度，并在基准测试和机载实验中验证。

title: Learning Side-by-Side Navigation for Personal Mobility Vehicles from Human Drivers
summary: This paper presents an approach to achieve side-by-side autonomous motion with a pair of personal mobility vehicles (PMVs). Given a global path, two PMVs plan cooperatively so as to hold a social formation that lets the passengers hold a conversation, while keeping the ride safe and smooth. Each vehicle runs its own sampling-based model-predictive planner; the planners exchange nothing but the odometry each vehicle could observe of the other, and the joint decision is expressed as a pair of utility matrices over pairs of candidate trajectories, resolved by a common rule. The behavioural parameters are fitted by inverse reinforcement learning from 409 minutes of driving by ten pairs of people in human-driven PMVs in an indoor environment, and the lanes the pair can use are derived offline from the corridor itself rather than fixed by hand. A safety layer the cost cannot override executes a move only if the vehicle can still brake clear, measured from its whole body, and a vehicle that is stuck reverses along its own path and continues. In closed-loop simulation over 24 runs in the conditions the drivers were recorded in and 24 in four generated obstacle layouts, no vehicle entered a wall or a cone. The pair holds conversational formation for 60.5 and 68.9 percent of the time among obstacles (anticlockwise and clockwise) and 81.2 and 91.5 percent in a clear aisle, against the drivers' 34.0 and 36.0 percent, and 52.9 and 56.0 percent, and it matches their speed. It keeps one lateral formation where the drivers alternated between a close diagonal and a wide abreast one, and it varies far less. Experimental results are based on a differential drive kinematic simulator running on ROS 2.
tldr: This paper presents a cooperative side-by-side navigation approach for pairs of personal mobility vehicles, using sampling-based model-predictive planners with inverse reinforcement learning to mimic human driving behavior, and validates it in simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于成对个人移动车辆并排导航的协作方法，通过采样模型预测规划器和逆强化学习模仿人类驾驶行为，并在仿真中验证。

title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
summary: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.
tldr: RESPLE2 is a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines, inertial-informed prediction, and global refinement with loop closures, achieving robust real-time odometry on various platforms including legged and aerial-legged robots.
tldr_zh: RESPLE2 是一种使用非均匀 B 样条的递归多传感器状态估计框架，通过惯性驱动的预测和全局回环优化，在包括腿式和空中腿式机器人等多种平台上实现了鲁棒的实时里程计。

title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution
summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are laboratory systems that couple experimental planning, automated execution, and measurement feedback in a closed loop. Integrating flexible robot control with the typed application programming interfaces (APIs) and continuous measurements exposed by laboratory instruments remains an execution-interface challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a traceable framework comprising four components: LAM (Lab Action Model), OpenSDL, Safe-SDL, and L3-Bench. LAM is a proposed measurement-conditioned policy architecture that extends vision-language-action paradigms to generate both continuous robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls. OpenSDL is an execution substrate with an initial control implementation, designed to map role-level operations to heterogeneous devices, coordinate execution, and record timestamped causal events. The proposed Safe-SDL runtime gate combines pre-dispatch schema and resource checks with signal temporal logic monitoring during execution, including extended waiting periods. L3-Bench (Level-3 Laboratory Benchmark) specifies an episode-level evaluation protocol covering physical outcomes, timing, reproducibility, safety violations, and fault recovery. Together, these components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.
tldr: The paper proposes a unified framework for Self-Driving Laboratories (SDLs) that integrates a vision-language-action model (LAM) for hybrid action generation, an execution substrate (OpenSDL), a safety runtime gate (Safe-SDL), and a benchmark (L3-Bench) to ensure auditable and safe autonomous experimentation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一个用于自驱动实验室（SDL）的统一框架，集成视觉-语言-动作模型（LAM）进行混合动作生成、执行基座（OpenSDL）、安全运行时门（Safe-SDL）以及基准测试（L3-Bench），以确保自主实验的可审计性和安全性。

title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
summary: Sparse event responses produce uneven keypoint errors whose effects on spacecraft pose depend on correspondence geometry and the reliability of successive observations. We present a reliability-aware framework connecting polarity--time localization, geometric recovery, event--CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization. A three-branch representation combines positive events, negative events, and recent-event timing through cross-branch attention and gating, followed by spatiotemporal aggregation. An ordered semantic-point head estimates relative correspondence precision for geometrically constrained pose recovery. Event-edge and CAD-projection agreement then guide local pose refinement under keypoint-geometry safeguards. At the sequence level, a ten-dimensional descriptor combines heatmap shape, reprojection consistency, and geometric conditioning to set time-aligned observation scales. On the official SPADES challenge test set, the complete system achieves a combined pose score of 0.0474, approximately 5.4\% below PASAN+IRIS. Validation ablations reduce the score from 0.0772 for base localization with uniform PnP to 0.0514 for the complete cascade; on identical single-frame observations, quality weighting reduces the score from 0.0549 with constant-weight optimization to 0.0514.
tldr: This paper presents a reliability-aware framework for event-based spacecraft pose estimation, integrating polarity-time localization, geometric recovery, event-CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization, achieving state-of-the-art results on the SPADES benchmark.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于事件相机的航天器姿态估计的可靠性感知框架，融合极性-时间定位、几何恢复、事件-CAD 精化和轨迹优化，在 SPADES 基准上取得了先进结果。

title: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
summary: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. This framework extends an established open-source state-of-the-art visual-inertial SLAM, SVIn, by integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into a tightly-coupled nonlinear optimiza- tion formulation resulting in improved estimates. To leverage the structural information of recently available 3D acoustic sonars while maintaining computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical architecture that incorporates estimates from a decoupled front-end via KISS-ICP, treated as relative pose factors within the factor graph. The proposed framework is validated through field deployments in a shipwreck and coral reef, demonstrating drift mitigation and global consistency. To support further research in underwater multi-modal fusion, the code and the datasets can be found on project website https://cmburgul.github.io/projects/svin+/ https://dartmouthrobotics.github.io/svin-plus
tldr: SVIn+ enhances underwater state estimation for AUVs by tightly integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into visual-inertial SLAM, and incorporating 3D sonar via a hierarchical architecture with KISS-ICP, validated in field deployments.
tldr_zh: SVIn+ 通过将水压和DVL测量紧密集成到视觉惯性SLAM中，并利用KISS-ICP的分层架构集成3D声纳，增强了AUV的水下状态估计，并在现场部署中验证了其漂移抑制和全局一致性。

title: Ground Sample Distance Constrained k-Coverage Viewpoint Planning via Set Multi-Cover Formulation
summary: Drone-based 3D reconstruction and inspection require viewpoints that satisfy image-quality constraints while observing each surface region multiple times, which overlap-based planning heuristics do not guarantee. We study ground sample distance (GSD)-constrained $k$-coverage viewpoint selection for structures represented by surface voxels. Candidate viewpoints are generated along outward surface directions, screened with distance, viewing-angle, field-of-view, and occlusion tests, and augmented for voxels with insufficient visibility. Selection is then posed as set multi-cover with per-voxel coverage demands. We propose a dynamically weighted greedy heuristic that prioritizes remaining coverage deficits and scarce viewing alternatives, and compare it with sequential overlap-based pruning and an integer linear programming (ILP) formulation on the same candidate pools. Across two structures, four voxel resolutions, and three coverage requirements, the proposed approach achieves full or near-full $k$-coverage with compact viewpoint sets, using only 3.00--16.39\% more viewpoints than ILP while offering an interpretable selection process based on coverage deficits and viewpoint availability.
tldr: This paper addresses GSD-constrained k-coverage viewpoint planning for drone-based 3D reconstruction by formulating it as a set multi-cover problem and proposing a dynamically weighted greedy heuristic that achieves near-optimal viewpoint sets efficiently.
tldr_zh: 本文针对无人机三维重建中的地面采样距离约束的k覆盖视点规划问题，将其建模为集合多重覆盖问题，并提出一种动态加权贪心启发式算法，能够以接近最优的视点数量实现全覆盖。

title: Compatibility and future-proof testing for multi-agent systems
summary: Independently developed autonomous agents, such as autonomous vehicles, must guarantee joint compatibility, such as safety and task-completion requirements, when they operate in a shared environment. Existing methods require a centrally designed specification, or interaction mechanism before any agent is deployed. However, such centralized design is unrealistic when agent designs are confidential to their developers, and it is not flexible enough to accommodate future agent designs. We study a bi-level structure in which a regulator coordinates developers by publishing seed agents, and each developer independently tests its agent to ensure that it is compatible with every seed-compatible agent, a property we call future-proofness. Under this structure, joint compatibility is guaranteed for any agents that are designed and tested independently, without any coordination with each other. In this work, we first formulate compatibility for general multi-agent systems and show why it is not trivially implied by seed-compatibility. We then characterize the future-proof agents as the closure of the seed and show that this closure is monotone in the seed. Finally, we study a class of executable tests that involve interaction with the seed alone, and we ask to what extent such tests can distinguish the future-proof agents.
tldr: This paper proposes a bi-level framework where a regulator publishes seed agents and developers independently test their agents for compatibility with all seed-compatible agents, ensuring future-proof joint compatibility in multi-agent systems without central coordination. It formalizes future-proofness, characterizes future-proof agents as the closure of the seed, and studies the limits of executable tests using only the seed.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种双层框架，由监管者发布种子智能体，开发者独立测试其智能体与所有种子兼容智能体的兼容性，从而在没有中央协调的情况下确保多智能体系统的联合兼容性。形式化了未来兼容性，将未来兼容智能体刻画为种子的闭包，并研究了仅使用种子的可执行测试的区分能力。

title: Understanding Human-Robot Collaboration through Joint Action
summary: Human-robot collaboration requires partners to coordinate interdependent contributions toward a shared goal. Joint Action theory provides concepts for understanding this coordination, but how these concepts are instantiated and combined across empirical research remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA 2020, identifying 83 empirical papers published between 2021 and 2026. Through theory-driven framework analysis, we organized the literature into nine constructs across three capacities: Representation, Prediction, and Integration. We analyze how these constructs are distributed and co-occur across studies, revealing where empirical evidence concentrates and where it is absent. By mapping empirical HRC research onto a unified Joint Action framework, this review offers a coherent overview of HRC studies, identifies gaps in current evidence, and provides guidelines for future research.
tldr: This paper presents a systematic review of human-robot collaboration literature, organizing 83 empirical studies into a unified Joint Action framework with nine constructs across three capacities. It identifies where empirical evidence is concentrated and absent, providing a roadmap for future HRC research.
tldr_zh: 本文对人机协作文献进行了系统综述，将83项实证研究组织到包含三个能力、九个构念的统一联合行动框架中，识别了实证证据的集中与缺失之处，为未来HRC研究提供了路线图。

title: Acoustic Signature Optimisation for Bioinspired Flapping-Wing Micro Aerial Vehicles
summary: Flapping-wing micro air vehicles are prized for quiet flight, yet the few existing measurements show engineered wings to be 15-30 dB louder than the animals they imitate. This paper investigates two passive geometric approaches to reduce the acoustic signature of a flapping membrane wing, and applies these to an exemplary wing. A significant sound source in flapping wings is the impulsive click radiated at stroke reversal, when a slack membrane snaps between two curvatures. Our first noise-reduction approach optimises the wing's venation layout, based on an analytical model of the reversal click as a dynamic snap-through of the membrane. The optimised venation pattern was manufactured and resulted in a reduction of up to 8 dB during the reversal snap in experiments. During testing, the venation was found to be sensitive to orientation rather than thickness. Secondly, an additive trailing-edge fringe inspired by hummingbird feathers was shown to further reduce the broadband swoosh by 3-4 dB at no lift cost, matching a cut serration wing without removing lifting area.
tldr: This paper optimizes the venation layout and adds a trailing-edge fringe to flapping-wing micro air vehicles, reducing acoustic noise by up to 8 dB at stroke reversal and 3-4 dB broadband without lift loss.
tldr_zh: 本文通过优化翼脉布局并添加尾缘锯齿，将扑翼微型飞行器的噪声降低了高达8分贝（换向时）和3-4分贝（宽带噪声），且不影响升力。

title: Integrated Design and Reproducible Feasibility Analysis of a Four-Wheel Rover with Packet-Commanded Imaging, LiDAR Ranging, and Learning-Assisted Target Recognition
summary: This study develops an integrated, reproducible design assessment for a four-wheel educational rover intended for the high-school remote-control division of the 2027 NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge. The architecture combines commercial differential drive control, independently sprung wheel carriers, separate drive and task batteries, and a Raspberry Pi-based subsystem that executes received imaging and ranging commands. The analysis reconciles component lists with dimensioned computer-aided design views, derives mobility and electrical constraints, and connects sensor geometry to command execution. At the estimated mass of 10.919 kg, a 215 mm wheel rotating at 200 RPM produces a theoretical rolling speed of 8.105 km/h; consequently, the nominal motor label does not establish compliance with an 8 km/h design ceiling. A steady 20-degree climb requires at least 1.255 newton-meters per wheel under an assumed rolling-resistance coefficient of 0.10 and equal torque sharing. At 50 ft, an ideal 12-inch feature spans approximately 71 pixels across a full-resolution Camera Module 3 Standard image, while a 1-degree pointing error displaces the ranging ray by approximately 266 mm. An executed synthetic benchmark compares color-geometry rules and two linear support-vector classifiers on 2,400 generated board crops with scene-disjoint evaluation. A separate reference command executor is checked using mocked hardware. These software results and analytical sensitivities support a testable development plan; the study does not report physical rover trials. The principal contribution is a traceable connection between component choices, failure mechanisms, quantitative design limits, and reproducible verification tasks.
tldr: This paper presents an integrated design and reproducible feasibility analysis for a four-wheel educational rover, combining mechanical, electrical, and software components with analytical sensitivities and synthetic benchmarks, but lacks physical trials.
tldr_zh: 本文对四轮教育机器人进行了一体化设计与可复现可行性分析，结合机械、电气和软件组件及分析敏感性和合成基准，但缺乏物理试验。

title: Gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-free guidance mechanism
summary: It is well established that some animals, such as sea turtles, sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a primary cue for long-distance navigation across the vast and featureless ocean. This remarkable ability has inspired the development of bio-inspired magnetic navigation (BIMN), which seeks to mimic these animals to develop robust and frugal navigation methods. BIMN exploits the Earth's magnetic field, sometimes described as ''Nature's GPS'', as a natural navigation infrastructure, providing a potential alternative to vulnerable satellite navigation systems. However, unlike geographic coordinates, magnetic coordinates extracted from the Earth's magnetic field do not provide a one-to-one mapping to geographic locations. Different locations can exhibit similar magnetic signatures, creating ambiguity and making BIMN inherently more challenging. Despite this fundamental challenge, we demonstrate that, within predefined regions of the Earth, magnetic inclination and intensity provide sufficient information to navigate to any destination. By formulating BIMN as a gradient flow control and guidance problem, we show that the resulting gradient flow act as current that carries the system and can be controlled to guide it through intermediate waypoints toward the desired destination. The resulting framework provides a GPS-free navigation mechanism with potential applications in both engineering and biology. In engineering, it can be used to establish a geomagnetic navigation infrastructure through which prescribed routes can be defined and followed, while in biology, it can be used to analyse the migration routes of animals known to rely on magnetoreception.
tldr: This paper proposes a GPS-free navigation mechanism based on the gradient flow of Earth's magnetic inclination and intensity, demonstrating that magnetic information is sufficient for navigation within predefined regions and offering applications in engineering and biology.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于地球磁倾角和磁强度梯度流的无GPS导航机制，证明了在预定义区域内磁信息足以实现导航，并为工程和生物学应用提供了可能。

title: A Singularity Avoiding Track Model for Race Car Optimization
summary: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. The surface is a Monge patch, parametrised by a curvilinear arc-length coordinate measured along the minimum-curvature line (MCL) and a signed lateral offset, with a height polynomial of user-selectable degree capturing the cross-sectional elevation profile. The choice of MCL as the reference line is deliberate since anchoring the same surface on the geometric centre-line can cause adjacent normals to cross inside the drivable region on tight corners. The resulting non-injective parametrisation assigns multiple curvilinear addresses to the same three-dimensional point and returns invalid road geometry. The MCL is obtained from a quadratic program that minimises integrated curvature subject to track-boundary, periodicity, and jerk-regularisation constraints. By reducing total curvature while remaining within the track bounds, the MCL moves the region of parametrisation breakdown outside the drivable strip on all circuits studied, keeps the normal map injective across the full track width, and yields a more linear time-to-arc-length transformation for minimum lap-time problems. The fitted surface and the associated track widths are exported as periodic piecewise-quintic $C^4$ B-splines, solved as a nonlinear program.
tldr: This paper presents a track fitting pipeline that converts measured racetrack point clouds into a singularity-free 3D surface model for race car optimization, using a minimum-curvature line to avoid parametrization breakdowns.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种赛道拟合流程，将测量点云转换为无奇异性的三维曲面模型，用于赛车优化，通过最小曲率线避免参数化失效。

title: A 2-DOF MultiBody Track Joint for Race Car Optimization
summary: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. The same FMU is then used for time-domain simulation and for CasADi/IPOPT minimum lap-time optimization, with no change to the model in between. This works because the joint keeps the arc-length coordinate as a real state and publishes its time derivative, which is the quantity that lets the problem be rewritten with distance We report results for minimum lap time simulations on the Singapore Formula~1 circuit.
tldr: This paper presents a Modelica MultiBody component, TrackJoint, that models a 2-DOF road constraint for race cars, enabling efficient simulation and optimization of minimum lap times on circuits like Singapore F1.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一个Modelica MultiBody组件TrackJoint，用于将三维路面建模为两自由度关节，实现赛车在赛道上的高效仿真和最小圈时优化。

title: Learning Human Sports Motion Feasibility via Quantile Regression on Tracking Data
summary: We study time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports: the shortest plausible time a player needs to reach an arbitrary location on the pitch given their current kinematic state, estimated as the lower envelope of observed locomotion times. Rather than modeling space ownership through position density estimation or closed-form physics-based models, we cast TTA as a conditional quantile regression problem, estimating the lower quantile of locomotion time so the model learns a player's lower-envelope arrival time. We train the model on optical tracking data from all 64 matches of the PFF FC FIFA World Cup 2022 dataset, and evaluate a lightweight multilayer perceptron against six player-motion models from the literature, re-expressed as TTA predictors, and a learned reachable- hull baseline. Across our evaluation metrics, the MLP consistently outperforms every physics-based baseline. To probe the generality of the learned locomotion model, we further evaluate it on basketball tracking data and a single-game NFL tracking dataset, analyzing the transferability of player motion dynamics across sports. Our project is available at https://github.com/mguti97/TTA-Quantile.
tldr: This paper uses quantile regression on sports tracking data to estimate the shortest plausible time for a player to reach any location on the field, proposing a lightweight MLP that outperforms physics-based models for motion feasibility prediction.
tldr_zh: 本文利用分位数回归技术，基于体育跟踪数据估计球员到达场地任意位置的最短合理时间，提出一种轻量级MLP模型，在运动可行性预测上优于基于物理的模型。

title: When Can a Learned Design Surrogate Be Trusted in a Self-Driving Microfluidics Laboratory? An Offline Closed-Loop Framework Built and Tested on Six Public Tables
summary: Self-driving laboratories couple a learned design surrogate to an instrument, and on every new target domain it must answer four questions: when it can be trusted, how many target measurements it needs, which to make first, and when to stop adapting, switch models or escalate. We state a framework making each measurable (a competence ratio, a budget $k^*(\varepsilon)$, a time-to-target and a priced decision) and instantiate it without wet experiments on six public droplet-microfluidic and liposome tables as offline laboratories: 107 leave-one-group tiers whose rows are hidden labels. A sealed, pre-registered programme (two sealed negative validations and a pre-registered test on three more tables) and seven frozen closed-loop protocols, each run twice, yield 23 findings. Shift cost is stratified by shift type; no label-free statistic certifies individual candidates; random-split model-family rankings predicted neither the sealed nor the loop rankings. Warm-start residual boosting returns a surrogate to $1.25\times$ its development reference within 20 target rows in 94% of chemistry tiers (27% under a strict noise-floor reading), 90% of laboratory and 40% of device tiers, and a budget planned from the shift type on other tables is not measurably worse on a new one. In the loop, one gain survives drift and shuffled-label controls on all tiers, carried by the sparsely sampled ones: proposing at once and warm-starting on every measurement reaches a 10% target in 2.80 measurements against 3.31 for the reference, and in 5.72 against 11.35 for random proposals on 301 hard units at a 3% tolerance. No label-free acquisition rule survives the shuffled-label control, no interval-aware proposal or other model family does better, and no threshold rule on the tested diagnostics beats always continuing once escalation is priced. No wet-lab validation is claimed.
tldr: This paper presents an offline closed-loop framework for self-driving microfluidics laboratories, addressing trust, budget, and adaptation decisions for learned design surrogates using six public datasets and pre-registered protocols.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于自驱动微流控实验室的离线闭环框架，基于六个公共数据集和预注册协议，解决学习设计代理的信任、预算和适应决策问题。

title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
summary: Electric-field-based actuators and machines lead the design space at the nanoscale and in biological systems, while having the potential to be used in favorable macroscale applications which prioritize minimal mass, performance in a vacuum, or performance in high temperatures. Electric-field induction motors consist of a set of stator electrodes which induce opposite charges onto a movable rotor surface. In earlier work, rotor surfaces for electric-field induction motors have been made of single continuum materials, which are limited in possible resistivity, permittivity and circuitry characteristics. To enhance design freedom, we develop a rotor for electric-field-based machines which may be constructed out of discrete circuit components between a finite number of conductive vanes. Magnetic-field induction motors, which are common in machinery, often utilize ``deep bar'' rotors, consisting of conducting bars which decrease the rotor time constant with increasing frequency using the skin depth effect. We propose, analyze, design and demonstrate a macro-scale electric-field induction motor which uses circuitry on the rotor surface to emulate the ``deep bar'' design, providing improved torque over a wide range of speeds.
tldr: This paper proposes a macro-scale electric-field induction motor with a rotor made of discrete circuit components to emulate 'deep bar' designs, improving torque across a wide speed range.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种宏观尺度的电场感应电机，其转子由分立电路元件构成，模拟“深槽”设计，在宽速度范围内提高扭矩。

title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation
summary: Coronary guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention requires continuous interpretation of vessel anatomy, guidewire position, and target stenosis under two-dimensional X-ray fluoroscopy. While existing approaches commonly address vessel segmentation or device localization as separate tasks, a robotic system requires a more structured perception of the coronary scene to support downstream navigation. In this work, we present a simulation-driven framework centered on a Multi-Task Coronary Perception Network (MCP-Net) for robotic guidewire navigation, integrating coronary vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation. Starting from three-dimensional coronary CT angiography, we generate simulated fluoroscopy images containing vascular structures, simulated guidewires, stenotic lesions with varying severity, and diverse vascular geometries, together with simulation-derived ground truth. MCP-Net jointly performs coronary vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization from a single fluoroscopic frame. These predictions are subsequently converted into a structured vascular graph containing centerlines, bifurcations, endpoints, branch directions, and branch angles. By associating the predicted stenosis with this graph, the framework generates a roadmap from the automatically selected graph root toward the target lesion. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can jointly recover coronary perception targets and transform them into an interpretable vascular representation suitable for downstream robotic navigation.
tldr: MCP-Net is a multi-task coronary perception network that jointly performs vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization from fluoroscopy, converting predictions into a structured vascular graph to generate a navigation roadmap for robotic guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention.
tldr_zh: MCP-Net是一种多任务冠状动脉感知网络，可从透视图像中联合进行血管分割、导丝尖端定位和狭窄定位，并将预测转换为结构化血管图，以生成用于机器人导丝导航的路线图。

title: A generalist policy for muscle-driven control across individual musculoskeletal models
summary: Differences in musculoskeletal morphology challenge policy reuse across individual models. Here we present MyoAcross, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning. Across 31 held-out individual models, MyoAcross achieves 99.24% completion and reduces tracking error by 22.60% relative to an unconditioned multilayer perceptron. Policy reuse extends to models of 22 held-out individuals constructed from single-image shape estimates, measured height and body mass, and, with asymmetry augmentation, to models with unilateral lower-limb shortening. Comparisons with measurements from 120 additional individuals show agreement in vertical ground reaction force waveforms and channel-dependent agreement between simulated muscle activations and electromyography. These results establish a common control framework for comparative simulations of movement across individual musculoskeletal models.
tldr: MyoAcross enables muscle-driven reference-motion tracking across individual musculoskeletal models without fine-tuning by combining model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning, and virtual data augmentation, achieving high completion and reduced errors on held-out individuals.
tldr_zh: MyoAcross通过结合个体肌肉骨骼模型构建、形态条件策略学习和虚拟模型增强，实现了无需微调的跨个体肌肉驱动参考运动跟踪，在保留个体上取得了高完成率和更低误差。

title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
summary: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead. Directly minimizing the prediction error over raw CSI coefficients is fragile in realistic propagation environments, since small-scale fading, mobility, local scattering, and small spatial perturbations can induce large phase-sensitive variations. Nevertheless, wireless channels contain strong spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain correlations that can be more predictably represented in a latent propagation-field domain. Motivated by this observation, we propose a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-inspired field world model, defined as a latent predictive model of the wireless propagation field, for sparse-pilot channel reconstruction. The model maps CSI observations into latent time-frequency tokens, predicts masked or future latent field states from historical multi-band context, and fuses the predicted latent prior with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full MIMO-OFDM channel. Ray-tracing experiments show that the proposed method improves normalized mean square error (NMSE) over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines, supporting latent field prediction as an effective prior for sparse-pilot channel acquisition.
tldr: The paper proposes a JEPA-inspired latent field prediction model for sparse-pilot MIMO-OFDM channel reconstruction, mapping CSI into latent time-frequency tokens and predicting masked/future states to fuse with sparse pilots, improving NMSE in ray-tracing experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种受JEPA启发的潜在场预测模型，用于稀疏导频MIMO-OFDM信道重建，将CSI映射为潜时间-频率令牌并预测掩蔽/未来状态，与稀疏导频融合，在射线追踪实验中提高了NMSE。

title: 3D-SceneQ: Empowering 3D LLM With Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning and Multi-Modal Feature Enhancement
summary: Current 3D scene understanding pipelines typically concatenate vast numbers of 3D object tokens with text tokens and feed the resulting sequence to a Large Language Model (LLM). However, existing 3D-LLMs for scene understanding encounter two major limitations: (i) excessive inclusion of task-irrelevant object data, introducing noise that reduces reasoning accuracy and increases hallucinations; and (ii) reliance solely on point cloud data, which inherently lacks the rich semantic information available in complementary 2D modalities, such as color, material properties, texture, and high-level contextual relationships. To address these challenges, we introduce 3D-SceneQ, a 3D LLM that unifies adaptive token pruning with multimodal semantic enrichment, markedly advancing scene understanding, reasoning, and grounding. Specifically, we propose a Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning (QGAP) module that adaptively selects task-relevant objects based on the intended meaning of user instructions, leveraging a learnable latent query to retain critical information while effectively suppressing irrelevant noise. In addition, we introduce a Multi-modal Object-level Feature Enhancement (MOFE) module, which integrates 2D feature embeddings from pre-trained models into 3D representation to enrich object-level semantic information. Evaluations show that 3D-SceneQ outperforms current state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks (e.g., +5.7 CIDEr on Scan2Cap and +17.0 EM@1 on SQA3D), demonstrating its remarkable capabilities in various 3D language reasoning tasks.

title: 4D Reconstruction with Events & RGB
summary: Reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes over time (4D reconstruction) from a single moving camera is central to robotics and AR/VR applications, yet state-of the-art feed-forward methods rely solely on RGB frames and therefore inherit the failure modes of conventional cameras, including motion blur and temporal aliasing under fast or non-uniform camera and object motion. Event cameras report per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously at microsecond resolution, offering a complementary signal that is largely immune to these artifacts, but whether this modality can be incorporated into existing RGB based 4D reconstruction pipelines without a full architectural redesign remains an open question. In this preliminary study, we investigate a minimal extension: we augment Monst3R, an existing RGB-only 4D reconstruction model, with an additional event-camera input branch, leaving the rest of the architecture unchanged. Across 3 benchmark datasets, this simple RGB-event fusion reduces Abs Rel by 3.4% on average relative to the RGB-only Monst3R baseline, and a sensitivity analysis shows that the improvement grows with the magnitude of camera and object motion, with the largest gains observed under high object motion conditions where RGB-only reconstruction degrades most. These early results suggest that even a lightweight, non-invasive fusion of event data can meaningfully improve 4D reconstruction robustness, motivating a more thorough architectural investigation in future work.

title: A First-Step Bias Restores Lost Diversity in Diffusion Model Distillation
summary: Distribution-matching distillation enables high-quality image generation in only a few denoising steps. However, distilled student models often map different initial noise samples to similar outputs under the same prompt. To locate where diversity is lost, we compare the teacher and student along the sampling trajectory. The largest measured reduction in the response to different initial noises occurs during the first, high-noise step. When we replace the first step with the teacher's corresponding trajectory and leave the final three student steps unchanged, most of the output diversity returns. This suggests that the first step is a key point for restoring diversity. Motivated by this finding, we introduce \emph{ReSeed}, a post-distillation method that adds a seed-response bias adapter only to the first student step and aligns its velocity with the teacher's first-interval secant velocity. All student weights and later denoising steps remain unchanged. We evaluate ReSeed on three text-to-image models (SD3-Medium, SD3.5-Medium, and FLUX.1-dev) and one text-to-video model (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B). For a distilled 4-step FLUX.1-dev model, \emph{ReSeed} requires only $0.00196\%$ additional trainable parameters relative to the base model and is trained on 8,000 prompt--noise pairs, while keeping the distilled student fully frozen and requiring no target images, perceptual losses, or adversarial losses. It improves DINO diversity by $48.3\%$ while maintaining competitive visual quality. These results show that substantial diversity can be recovered through a lightweight, data-efficient tuning of only the first denoising step, without finetuning the full student model.

title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs
summary: Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. In visual communication between models, this leads to a generation--interpretation gap: while models tend to send shape primitives that they (and humans) find intuitive, these visual cues often fail to steer other models. In further communication games involving abstract concepts and stories, models can creatively use visuals to transmit meaning to one another, although some communications remain non-intuitive to humans. These findings reveal that VLMs might be capable of rich, creative, and visually-grounded communication, but their interpretation and production of visual meaning diverges from human conventions in surprising ways. Together this work highlights both the promise and challenges of visual communication between humans and VLMs.

title: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN with Saliency-Map Interpretability for Skin Cancer Detection
summary: Skin cancer is among the most prevalent and life threatening forms of cancer worldwide. Early and accurate diagnosis significantly improves patient survival rates. However, manual dermoscopic assessment remains challenging due to visual similarity. This study proposes an Explainable AI-driven framework for automated binary classification of skin lesions using a lightweight attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN-Attention). The model integrates channel attention to focus on informative regions of dermoscopic images while maintaining low computational complexity. A publicly available dataset comprising 2,637 training and 660 test images was used, with balanced class weights. The proposed model achieved 87 percent accuracy with 1.95 million parameters and 7.45 MB of storage, matching the best baseline (MobileNet) while using approximately half as many parameters and half as much storage. ROC AUC and PR AUC scores reached 0.9475 and 0.9430, respectively. Additionally, saliency maps were incorporated as an explainability technique to visualize regions that influence model decisions. Comparative analysis with VGG16,VGG19,ResNet101,and MobileNet demonstrates the proposed models effectiveness in balancing classification results, computational efficiency, and interpretability.

title: A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models
summary: The Asch conformity experiment has recently gained considerable attention as a way of measuring conformity in large language models (LLMs). While previous studies have focused on demonstrating conformity in LLMs, our work adds a further quantitative layer to this approach. Instead of sampling a frontier LLM on a suite of questions, our approach samples a single question repeatedly, leveraging the probabilistic nature of LLMs to produce a distribution of answers. In doing so, we can compare the distributions of answers before and after the model is presented with the manufactured consensus. Our experiments confirm that frontier LLMs do conform, reinforcing prior literature, and, through our distribution-to-distribution comparisons, provide additional quantitative data on the conditions that lead to conformity and the degree to which it occurs.

title: A Simple Presentation of Robust Membership Inference Attacks
summary: In a membership inference attack, an attacker is given the data of a particular individual, and tries to determine if that individual was included in a particular dataset, given some kind of statistics derived from the dataset or a model trained on the dataset. Roughly, a membership inference attack is robust if it succeeds even when the statistics are highly noisy, regardless of how that noise is introduced. We give a simple presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation, covering both multivariate Gaussian distributions and binary product distributions. We also give a summary of the literature on robust membership inference, covering history, extensions, and connections to other research areas.

title: A Smart Instant Book Filter Model based on Dual-Objective Optimization
summary:
Hospitality service in online marketplaces has become increasingly popular over the past few years, not only because it helps people easily rent short-term lodging but also because it empowers travelers to connect with locals and feel belonging. A typical pattern of these industries is a central platform mediating the economic interactions between guests and hosts, where a successful booking experience is the key to user satisfaction. However, one of the biggest challenges is the possible delay of response and chance of rejection when guests try to book a request-to-book listing. Previously, we enabled the instant book feature to allow hosts to instantly accept qualified guests and guests to confirm bookings immediately. Yet the symptom has not been alleviated given mixed request-to-book and instant book listing supply in search results. One possible solution is to promote all instant book listings in search results; however, booking rate will be damaged due to some improperly promoted low quality listings.
  In this paper, we present a novel smart instant book filter system that applies the instant book filter intelligently and shifts request-to-book to instant book without hurting booking rate. Compared with traditional two-sided markets research that targets finding strategies to maximize a single overall social welfare goal, our proposed system aims to maximize the instant book rate with the constraint that booking rate should not decrease, forming a dual-objective optimization problem.
  We show A/B testing results for our system exposed to global users, demonstrating that our model performs better than previous human-expert-tuned models in terms of both instant book rate and overall booking rate. We also achieved improved metrics such as the host instant book adoption rate. The proposed system has been deployed to production and is serving millions of users every day.

title: A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models
summary: Adapting foundation models to a new task within or beyond the training domain is the de facto standard for building specialized machine learning models. Recently, Visual Prompting (VP) has emerged as a promising technique for efficient knowledge transfer. As new foundation model families~(like Mamba) get introduced and VP pipelines such as AutoVP reach greater maturity, we find a growing need for a systematic evaluation of current approaches. In this work, we assess the performance of the latest models, comparing them to earlier architectures and alternative fine-tuning methods, to better understand the progress, challenges and opportunities in the field of efficient fine-tuning under resource limitations. Towards this goal, this paper provides a concise empirical overview of the interactions among foundation model families (Attention-, Convolution-, and Mamba-based) and transfer paradigms: VP, Linear Probing (LP), Full Fine-tuning (FFT) and Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Our work builds up on previous findings by broadening the selection of evaluated models and techniques while tuning hyperparameters. In the interest of delivering practical guidelines for the user, we also explore application of prevalent regularization techniques to boost performance in the context of VP.

title: AC-JEPA: Anchored Cross-Modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Visual-to-Symbolic Translation
summary: Cross-modal translation requires models to capture shared semantics across modalities while preserving the fine-grained structure required by the target modality. Yet in real-world scientific domains, paired data are often imperfect, while obtaining clean pairs at scale is costly. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) directly optimizes cross-modal translation through categorical token-level supervision, but this objective is sensitive to errors in the target sequences. JEPA offers a complementary representation-space objective, but most existing formulations focus on prediction within a modality rather than translation across modalities. We introduce Anchored Cross-Modal JEPA (AC-JEPA), an SFT-compatible plug-in that predicts masked intermediate states in both cross-modal directions using paired data. The joint-embedding objective targets cross-modal structure predictable from context, while the causal SFT path retains direct token-level supervision for the target sequence. During self-training, AC-JEPA learns from continuous latent targets derived from imperfect pseudo-labeled pairs, offering intrinsic tolerance to local data errors without promoting pseudo-tokens to hard categorical supervision. Using optical chemical structure recognition as a testbed, AC-JEPA trained on clean pairs achieves 76.07% accuracy on the Simple set of the WildMol benchmark, compared with 67.40% for SFT alone. Using the same pseudo-labeled data for both approaches, AC-JEPA-based self-training further raises accuracy to 80.23%, whereas accuracy under direct SFT drops from 67.40% to 63.47%. These results support SFT-anchored joint-embedding prediction as an effective strategy for cross-modal translation under both curated and imperfect supervision.

title: ADTGuard: Adaptive Depth-Time Safeguard for Streaming Inference in Large Language Models
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate fluent responses to diverse user requests, yet streaming may expose users to harmful content before generation is complete. Existing guardrails face two limitations in this setting. First, post-hoc moderation at response or chunk boundaries delays intervention, risking harmful exposure when content is released before verification. Second, even with token-level detection, coarse response-level supervision does not specify when harmful content begins, while fixed-layer readouts may miss relevant safety signals at other depths. To address these limitations, we introduce ADTGuard, which checks each token before release, progressively refines token-level training targets, and adapts layer selection to the current prefix. ADTGuard models risk across depth and time through Depth-Time Safety Dynamics (DTSD), which integrates safety evidence across layers at each token and uses it to guide risk accumulation over successive tokens. To adapt the choice of observation layers to the current prefix, we propose the Causal Depth Router (CDR). With only response-level labels available, we further develop Risk-Onset Target Refinement (RTR) to progressively construct token-level training targets for both components. Through extensive experiments across multiple safety benchmarks, we demonstrate that ADTGuard consistently achieves strong streaming detection performance, matching or surpassing state-of-the-art safeguards while requiring only 16M trainable parameters and maintaining competitive per-token latency.

title: AHEAD: Adaptive Neural Acceleration for Large-Scale Linear Programming
summary: Large-scale linear programs with millions of variables and constraints strain time and memory budgets. First-order methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient scale to this regime because they avoid matrix factorizations, but they require many iterations. Learned accelerators can reduce these iterations, yet fewer iterations do not guarantee a shorter solve. Learning inference also takes time, and running the accelerator longer trades solver time for inference time.
